verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left arm numbness, tingling, and weakness for at least 2 weeks: "it's probably been, I'd say, for at least two weeks, and it's kind of gotten worse... then the numbing kind of started... as well as in my hand" and confirms weakness: "it's, like, numb, I can't feel it" and difficulty using the arm.

Paresthesia in palmar aspect of 2nd–4th digits and numbness at rest are described: "OK, so it's my second, third, and fourth finger" and "It's, it's the, it's this side. So, the front side" and "if i'm just like resting... I can feel like it's numb, and I... feel, tingling right now". Occasional shoulder ache: "sometimes I will feel it in my shoulder... maybe feel a little bit of... pain."

Symptoms affect fine motor tasks and imply grasp issues: "I play a little bit of a piano and so I just noticed it's been kind of harder to get the notes" and discussion of weakness vs pain when holding objects: doctor asks about dropping a glass; patient says she mainly uses right hand but agrees it's numb rather than painful.

Temporal association with boxing: "I've been taking this boxing class for a few weeks" and "Well, I guess because of this. You know, I'm not sure if it's boxing"; onset during the period after starting boxing and she links it as a possible cause.

Massage and hot baths did not help: "I tried to get a massage, it's not better. Or, you know, try to take warm baths. It's not better". Ibuprofen did not relieve the numbness: she took ibuprofen for sore muscles/knuckles and still sought care for persistent numbness, indicating no relief for that symptom.

Denies neck pain, seizures, and leg weakness: Neck pain – "Edward, any neck pain at all?" Patient initially says "Yes, absolutely" then corrects: "No, not, no, nothing". Seizures – "you've not experienced anything like a seizure... ?" Patient: "Ohh, no, no, no, no, nothing like that". Leg weakness – "weakness is only in your left arm. Legs are walking... normal, yeah?" Patient: "Yeah, yeah, yeah, walking is normal".

Transient peripheral visual loss in left eye after viral illness: "I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago" and later "another weird thing... I all of a sudden just couldn't see... from my left eye... I lost some... field of vision"; duration ~20 minutes: "that just lasted maybe for, I don't know, twenty, twenty minutes?" and repeated later as about twenty minutes.

Fatigue-related headaches: "sometimes I get headaches but I think they're just tired headaches" and links to overwork/exhaustion: "I think that's probably because I work too much... or... I'll really just exhaust myself and then I just kind of feel this fatigue."
Recent severe cold/flu: "I also had a really bad cold, like a month ago" and "I was sick for probably good like two weeks... I think I must have had some kind of like a flu or something."

Medication use: "I do take Ibuprofen because my muscles were sore" and later: "Not really. I just take ibuprofen every once in a while, I take vitamin D. Um, I take some... iron supplements, but... most of the time I just forget... And then, sometimes I take Melatonin to help me sleep." This matches ibuprofen PRN, vitamin D, infrequent iron, and melatonin PRN.
Father’s conditions: "I know that my dad has I don't know if it it's hypo, I think it's hypothyroidism" and "he's got some autoimmune stuff going on, like that much I know."
Mother’s conditions: "my mom... she's got diabetes type two. She's got hypertension, um, she's got, gosh, what is it, ohh, yeah, she's got high cholesterol." Hyperlipidemia = high cholesterol.

Supported: regular exercise/boxing – "I work out" and "I've been taking this boxing class"; right-hand dominant – "I use my right hand most of the time, you know, I'm not left handed"; no glasses/contacts – "Do you wear glasses at all... ?" "No". Not supported: alcohol pattern is described only as a single episode of heavy drinking ("we were like out partying... uncharacteristically drunk"), not routine occasional heavy use; smoking status is never discussed. Thus parts about alcohol pattern and being a non-smoker are additions.

The note’s differential (demyelinating process, cervical radiculopathy, or overuse injury) is not explicitly listed. Doctor mentions only concern about "something a bit more than just the boxing" and specifically "things like MS, multiple sclerosis"; cervical radiculopathy and overuse injury as diagnostic labels are not stated.

Doctor does not name optic neuritis as the cause of visual loss. He links visual problems generally to MS: "people with multiple sclerosis can have, um, visual problems, like what you've experienced" but does not say optic neuritis.

Possible MS requiring urgent evaluation: "sometimes you know you do get things like MS, multiple sclerosis" and "I'm not suggesting that you do have it, but it is quite important to find out whether you have it or not" and "I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral."

Supported: urgent neurology referral – "I'm going to do an urgent, very urgent neurology referral." Not supported/contradicted: specific plan for MRI of brain and spine is not mentioned; doctor only says "What that might entail is the brain scan and things like that" without specifying spine imaging or definitively ordering MRI.

Doctor educates about possible MS, early diagnosis, and steroids: explains MS and its symptoms; reassures about treatment: "if we capture it a bit early there are treatments for it" and later: "The treatment for it is actually some steroids and things like that... But... first we need to firm diagnosis."

ED/return precautions: "while you're waiting... if the weakness progresses to your legs, or there's any kind of headaches, vomiting, fits, and your visual symptoms are getting worse and not getting better, then that would be an A and E." This covers worsening weakness, visual changes, severe headache, vomiting, and seizures (fits).

Doctor says no new treatment now: "No, that's something we can't do" regarding drugs for MS, and does not explicitly instruct to continue ibuprofen; prior ibuprofen use is only described by patient. The statement "Continue over-the-counter ibuprofen as needed" is a new instruction not given in the transcript.

Doctor arranges urgent referral but there is no explicit plan stated to follow-up after imaging/results: he says "hopefully we'll get things sorted and the ball rolling" but does not specify a scheduled follow-up once neurology/imaging is done.
